text:
owen: RFC idea — run a focused 'kernel-slice' benchmark to compare kernel selection + batching across long-context, prefill-heavy mixes. goal: apples-to-apples where we keep model weights and hw constant and only vary runtime kernel choices and batching heuristics. quick sketch below.

maya: +1. this feels overdue with the recent regressions. can you outline the workloads and measurables?

owen: sure. workloads: 1) prefill-dominant chat sim (avg prefill 6k, tail to 32k), 2) mixed sessions (50% short, 30% mid, 20% long), 3) pure long tail (90% >16k). measure: p50/p90/p99 latency per token, tokens/sec, GPU util, kernel time breakdown (attention vs matmul vs memory ops), and effective batch size distribution.

liam: how do we ensure "apples-to-apples"? seeds + deterministic replay harness?

owen: two parallel tracks: A) replay harness using recorded traffic from long-context customers (sanitized) to validate realism, B) synthetic sampler with explicit seqlen distribution to sweep params. both runs pinned to same model release, same node pool id, and controlled background noise (no other jobs).

maya: please add KV cache hit/miss metrics. prefill workloads are sensitive to prefix caching. we should capture KV memory pressure and eviction counts.

owen: good call. will add: kv_hits, kv_misses, kv_evictions, avg_kv_key_size, and peak_kv_mem.

perf-bot: [automation] scheduled perf job created: kernel-slice/1987654321-run-1 (see CI link) :robot_face:

liam: what about comparing kernel variants? we have: kernel-v1 (float16 fused), kernel-v2 (int8 quantized), kernel-v2-slowpath (fallback for long seqs), and aten baseline. we need a matrix.

owen: propose matrix: each workload x kernel variant x batching policy {aggressive-batcher, conservative, prefills-only}. keep model and hw constant.

maya: batching policy details? define thresholds and timeouts please.

owen: rough defs: aggressive = max_batch=1024, batch_timeout=10ms; conservative = max_batch=192, batch_timeout=2ms; prefills-only = allow large batch only if request is prefill (we detect via header). will finalize.

liam: detection heuristic for prefill header can be fuzzed by clients. add a fallback metrics tag so we can filter run segments that were mis-tagged.

owen: noted. we'll emit tag:prefill_detected:true/false per request in traces.

maya: logging/trace level — we need per-token kernel attribution. can we get stack traces for hotspots?

owen: runtime can emit kernel level timing per step. example snippet we'll collect in traces:```json
{"step": 512, "attention_ms": 12.3, "matmul_ms": 3.1, "kv_lookup_ms": 0.8, "overhead_ms": 1.5}```

liam: how long will each run be? we need steady-state — at least 30 minutes per cell or until 200k tokens. pick whichever is longer.

owen: agree. set min_duration=30m, min_tokens=200000.

maya: about hardware: run on a homogeneous pool (A100-80GB) and separately on a densified T4 pool to see memory/quant tradeoffs. confirm GPU util threshold for valid runs (>=40% avg).

owen: will schedule both pools. validation: avg_gpu_util >= 40% else mark as noisy and rerun.

perf-bot: [run status] kernel-slice/1987654321-run-1 queued on pool: a100-80g.

liam: for analysis, produce apples-to-apples charts: normalized tokens/sec vs kernel variant (v1 baseline=1.0), p99 delta heatmap, and kv_eviction vs p99. also export raw traces for perf team.

owen: yep. output artifacts: summary.csv, kernel_breakdown.parquet, replay_o11y_trace.jsonl, charts.pdf.

maya: we should add a regression detector: if p99 latency increases >10% vs baseline for any kernel variant on same workload, flag and create issue.

owen: added to checklist. automation will create GH issue with diffs and attach kernel_breakdown.

liam: one more: randomize request arrival patterns within each workload (poisson vs burst) to exercise batching heuristics.

owen: good call — include poisson lambda tunables + burst parameter.

maya: can you draft the actual job YAML and CI entry? I'll review and sanity-check thresholds.

owen: will post YAML in next message. thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: [automation] job created: ci/perf/kernel-slice/1987654321 (auto-retry=2)
